executive_summary: Union Bank’s September quarter combines improving spreads and asset quality with a substantial mismatch between loan and deposit growth. The stock’s near-book valuation looks less demanding than premium private banks, but the sustainability of returns depends on funding discipline and ECL buffers rather than simply extrapolating the present low credit cost.
research_stance: Positive operating recovery with a funding constraint to monitor; balance valuation appeal against late-benign asset quality.

thesis_drivers.title: Profitability is rebuilding on operating metrics
thesis_drivers.evidence: The latest official call reports NIM 2.86%, up from 2.80%, RoA 1.38% and RoE 17.21%. These standalone bank metrics support a more durable recovery thesis than consolidated PAT alone.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and latest earnings-call transcript

thesis_drivers.title: Cleanup supports capital generation
thesis_drivers.evidence: GNPA 2.42%, NNPA 0.42%, PCR 95.20% and credit cost 21 bps point to a benign current credit environment. Lower provisions help returns, but the next credit cycle is unlikely to improve indefinitely from this base.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and latest earnings-call transcript

thesis_drivers.title: Deposit growth is the binding test
thesis_drivers.evidence: Advances grew 18.53% YoY versus deposits 6.87%; management says CASA plus retail term deposits contribute 80.3% of deposits. Stable average liquidity matters more than quarter-end balances, but continued divergence would raise marginal funding cost.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and latest earnings-call transcript

industry_context.heading: Bank-specific framework
industry_context.content: Assess NII, NIM, deposits, asset quality, capital and RoA/RoE. The local consolidated table intentionally has no industrial sales, EBITDA or OPM; those blanks are not operating weakness.

industry_context.heading: Competitive position
industry_context.content: A large public-sector franchise combines branch-led distribution and a broad loan book with state ownership and a lower valuation. Compare return durability and deposit costs rather than applying a uniform PSU discount or private-bank premium.

industry_context.heading: Macro read-through
industry_context.content: A rate increase can lift floating-rate asset yields before deposit repricing, while simultaneously increasing borrower stress and market losses. The earnings benefit is time dependent, not automatic.

valuation.method: Reverse valuation and sustainable-return constraints; point target withheld
valuation.assessment: Snapshot valuation is 1.07× book and 7.05× earnings, with snapshot RoE 15.7%. Latest standalone call RoE 17.21% is a different period/scope; do not mix it into an exact justified-P/B model. A valuation near book is attractive only if normalised RoE remains above cost of equity.
assumptions: A full P/ABV requires deduction of unprovided NPAs, ECL and subsidiary valuation reconciliation.
The previous arbitrary bear/base/bull target-price sensitivities have been removed. The deeper valuation discussion states the economic return conditions and analyst assumptions instead.

bull: NIM remains near 2.8–2.9% while deposits catch up to credit demand.
Strong internal capital generation absorbs ECL transition and supports profitable growth.
Asset quality remains benign enough for a sustained premium to book.
base: Loan growth moderates or deposit pricing rises to restore funding balance.
RoA remains above 1% but present recoveries and credit costs normalise.
Valuation tracks sustainable bank returns rather than the fastest quarterly PAT growth.
bear: Funding competition erodes NIM as loan growth outruns deposits.
ECL or fresh slippages consume more capital than current buffers can absorb.
A PSU-bank discount returns if execution or underwriting weakens.

quality_assessment.business: Scaled deposit and credit franchise with improving profitability; funding growth currently trails opportunities.
quality_assessment.management: October call gives concrete liquidity and credit metrics, but confidence must be tested against subsequent deposit mobilisation.
quality_assessment.capital_allocation: CET1 of 16.05% offers headroom; use it to fund risk-adjusted lending and ECL transition, not simply maximise growth.
quality_assessment.governance: A state-owned bank with a rapidly growing loan book needs explicit accountability for underwriting and liability mobilisation. The large loan/deposit growth gap makes average liquidity, deposit concentration and risk-adjusted lending disclosure more useful than optimistic terminal growth.
quality_assessment.limitations: Consolidated local PAT and standalone call PAT differ by perimeter; bank operating KPIs are management-reported, not all present in the parquet.

business_economics: Union’s immediate opportunity is to convert a large funding and distribution franchise into higher-quality earning assets without sacrificing funding economics. Loan growth of 18.53% versus deposit growth of 6.87% makes the source, tenor and cost of new liabilities a central thesis variable.

Management cites approximately 120% average LCR, around 84% domestic credit-deposit ratio and longer-tenor FCNR funding. These show available funding tools and current liquidity comfort, but do not demonstrate that incremental asset growth has the same risk-adjusted return as the legacy book.
earnings_quality: Standalone PAT of ₹5,537 crore and ROA of 1.38% are stronger headline numbers than the approximately 1.03% core ROA management reports after treasury/TWO adjustments. Both belong in the analysis: the former measures reported outcomes, the latter tests dependence on recoveries and treasury. The local ₹5,781 crore consolidated PAT has a wider perimeter.

GNPA/NNPA of 2.42%/0.42% and credit cost of 21 basis points are current conditions. Loan growth, mix changes and low credit costs can coexist before new vintages season; monitor slippages and Stage 2/SMA migration rather than credit cost alone.
capital_allocation: Management’s approximate ₹5,500 crore total ECL transition estimate is partly offset by ₹1,000 crore additional buffer. Treating the full ₹5,500 crore as an incremental unbuffered charge exaggerates the day-one burden, but assuming the transition buffer also solves every recurring ECL cost is equally wrong.

The bank can fund growth using deposits, refinance, infrastructure/green bonds and other capital instruments. The economic test is not whether the balance sheet can grow at all; it is whether marginal funding spreads and capital consumption preserve core returns after provisioning.
valuation_logic: The dated snapshot P/B is 1.07 x and ROE is 15.7%. A deliberately simplified perpetual-bank identity, P/B=(ROE −g)/(cost of equity −g), using analyst assumptions of 13% cost of equity and 6% long-run growth, would require a steady-state ROE of about 13.5% at that book multiple. This is a diagnostic of the earnings expectations in the price, not a fair value, forecast or calibrated discount rate. A changing growth phase, subsidiary values, adjusted book and surplus capital can materially alter the answer.

Union’s approximately 1.07 x snapshot book value is lower than KVB’s 2.40 x and ICICI’s 2.93 x, but those franchises differ in funding mix, sustainable returns and subsidiary value. The discount is an opportunity only if the bank retains a core return above its required equity return through a less benign credit environment. No target P/ABV is supplied without adjusted-book and ECL reconciliation.
peer_positioning: Bank of India is a closer public-sector comparison than KVB or ICICI for ownership and broad funding characteristics. Its dated snapshot P/B of 0.74 x and ROE of 12.4% compare with Union’s 1.07 x and 15.7%, suggesting that the market already differentiates return quality. These are dated consolidated snapshot ratios, not a synchronized standalone peer-return study.
